html:
The Waxhaw were a Siouan speaking people of the Piedmont on the border of the Carolinas, around what are now Lancaster County, South Carolina, and Union County, North Carolina.

The English explorer John Lawson visited them in 1701 and described their custom of flattening the foreheads of infants. They were close to the Catawba and Sugaree. The Waxhaw were nearly destroyed in the Yamasee War of 1715, and survivors joined the Catawba. The region kept their name, the Waxhaws, where Andrew Jackson was born in 1767.
